elements.element: Commerce One shall maintain commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no commercial general liability insurance requirement.

elements.element: Commerce One shall maintain commercial general liability insurance with an aggregate limit of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no commercial general liability aggregate limit.

elements.element: Commerce One shall maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: The clause requires professional liability insurance of only USD 1,000,000.

elements.element: If Commerce One processes Customer Data, Commerce One shall maintain cyber/privacy insurance of at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: The condition that Commerce One does not process Customer Data is not demonstrably absent, and the clause requires only USD 2,000,000 of cyber liability and privacy insurance.

elements.element: Commerce One shall maintain workers' compensation insurance as required by law.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no workers' compensation insurance requirement.

elements.element: Commerce One shall provide certificates of insurance upon request.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no obligation to provide certificates of insurance upon request.

elements.element: Commerce One shall maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly requires Commerce One to maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000.

elements.element: Commerce One shall maintain cyber/privacy insurance of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly requires Commerce One to maintain cyber liability and privacy insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000.

result.reason: The operative language fully implements the stated fallback limits but omits the preferred CGL, workers' compensation, and certificate requirements and uses lower E&O and cyber/privacy limits. The change is limited to the fallback requirements and does not disturb the existing bankruptcy or integration provisions. Drafting quality is reduced because the new unnumbered insurance provision appears after the agreement's execution language rather than as a properly numbered substantive section.
